question_en: Which water supply facility, and in which city, is documented in this set of historical survey photographs?
answer: Matsumoto City; 鉄道給水源跡 (Railway Water Supply Source Site)
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 2-2-C01

## Step 01 · Treat the two photos as pending clues for the same facility

**Action:** Record visible information from the street view and the underground space separately. Try using terms like `中信オートリース 給水 跡` and `レンガ 地下 給水 調査` to access Japanese local survey materials; the reading of the signboard still requires verification by other evidence.

**Evidence Observation:** The first image shows a survey scene on a Japanese street, featuring Japanese signboards, utility poles, a roadside stone monument, and a long ladder, with people pixelated; the prominent vertical sign can be identified as "中信オートリース". The second image shows a large rusted valve body within a brick-walled space, with components extending along the base of the wall and a metal ladder on the right. The brick-built space and the valve support the hypothesis of a water supply facility, but the brick wall alone cannot determine the city, era, or whether it was used for railways. The signboard is not the facility name, and the merchant's address cannot be directly taken as the answer to the question.

**Result of this step:** Prioritize searching for local cultural property reports containing photos of underground brick-built water sources and valves; use city clues only to narrow the search, not to replace verification against the same images.

## Step 02 · Connect the description of Matsumoto's railway water source with the survey report

**Action:** Check the "鉄道給水源跡" page on the Matsumoto City Cultural Properties Division website and access the "《鉄道給水源跡記録保存調査報告書》" (Railway Water Supply Source Site Record Preservation Survey Report) linked on that page. Use `松本 レンガ 地下 給水` or `松本 鉄道 給水源 調査` to further locate this material.

https://www.city.matsumoto.nagano.jp/soshiki/134/158897.html

https://www.city.matsumoto.nagano.jp/uploaded/attachment/104418.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The archived municipal government page explains that a brick-built well combined with a water tank was constructed in the Umaibashi area, utilizing elevation differences to supply water to Matsumoto Station, located about 1.5 km away. The city map on the 4th physical PDF page of the report marks both Matsumoto Station and the "鉄道給水源跡", and the survey background on page 7 also explains the relationship between the water source and the station. At this point, the name, city, and facility type are consistent with the clues, but it must still be confirmed that the photos are indeed of this specific location; an answer cannot be given solely based on matching keywords.

**Result of this step:** Obtained an official report with a clearly defined survey subject; proceed to compare photos within the document.

## Step 03 · Locate the two input photos on the same report page

**Action:** View the 42nd physical PDF page of the report (which corresponds to printed page 39) and compare the street view in the upper left and the side view of the valve in the lower left with the input images.

https://www.city.matsumoto.nagano.jp/uploaded/attachment/104418.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The utility pole vertical sign, background buildings, stone monument, and roadside ladder in the upper-left photo correspond to the non-pixelated parts of the first input image; the pixelation of people is a result of input processing and should not be treated as a different scene from the original report. The lower-left photo corresponds to the second input image in terms of the rusted outline of the valve body, its position against the wall, the components extending along the wall base, the ladder on the right, and the layout of debris on the ground. Its caption describes it as a horizontal view of the water supply valve on the west side, facing towards the station. The joint appearance of both photos on the same survey page establishes the identity of the entity more directly than a single similar valve or a blurry signboard.

**Result of this step:** Both input images are matched with the survey photos of this railway water supply source in Matsumoto City; the target is the water supply source site, not the Matsumoto Station building itself or a water tower inside the station.

## Step 04 · Address the boundary between similarly named wells and historical photos

**Action:** Verify the location background using page 3 of the Nagano Prefecture Buried Cultural Properties Center publication, and check the similarly named `Source Well at the Water Source Site` on the official Matsumoto tourism page to avoid conflating English names that are similar.

https://naganomaibun.or.jp/uploads/f7762b3ea596df5713769403f9e5195f.pdf

https://visitmatsumoto.com/en/spot/detail_1075.html

**Evidence Observation:** The title of the prefectural archaeological publication is directly "松本市 鉄道給水源跡" (Matsumoto City Railway Water Supply Source Site), accompanied by a location map, photos of the brick interior, and some preserved site photos, which aligns with the railway water supply background of the report; it shares common surveyor backgrounds with the city report and cannot be called a completely independent site survey. In contrast, the similarly named tourism entry specifies the address as 1-1 Chuo 4-chome and describes well water for human consumption, which cannot explain the railway water tank shown in the report for this question. Archived municipal data also states that the facility has long been out of service, with above-ground parts demolished and underground remains removed; therefore, the images in the question are used only to identify the historical survey subject, not to infer that it remains fully preserved in its current state.

**Result of this step:** The city, specific facility name, and historical context have all been determined; there is no need to continue traversing all wells in Matsumoto.

## Step 05 · Provide the city and facility name

**Action:** Provide both the city and the original facility name as required by the question.

**Evidence Observation:** Answering only "Matsumoto" fails to specify the water supply facility; answering only "railway well" lacks the proper name. The same images in the report and materials on the city location jointly support the following answer.

**Result of this step:** Stop searching.

**Formal Answer:**

Matsumoto City; 鉄道給水源跡
